subject: Radar · A 1-gram robot flies alone · Week of 23 Nov
html:
An insect-sized flying robot steers itself, solar models are tested on unseen data, and AI that sees and reads.
TECH RADAR
A robot the weight of a paperclip learns to fly on its own
Weekly edition no. 33 · Week of Monday 23 November 2026 (papers from the last 7 days) · about 9 minutes
 
IN 30 SECONDS
1An insect-scale flying robot from MIT hovered and dodged obstacles using only its own sensors and computer, a step toward tiny drones that can work outside the lab.
2In energy, a Jülich team proposes a simple test for solar-cell models: can they predict measurements they were never fitted to? This matters as machine learning speeds up materials research.
3AI that combines images and text is the fastest-rising topic in the LLM vertical, and two reviews this week map its weak spots: adapting to new domains and inventing answers when checking photos.

new papers indexed this week in the 5 verticals
290
of them published during the week

research momentum of LLMs and generative AI this year
SIGNAL OF THE WEEK
A 1.29-gram flying robot that senses and steers by itself
Science Robotics · Published 18 Nov 2026  Journal  High-impact journal
Who wrote it: Hsiao Yi-Hsuan and 8 others · Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cornell University (United States) · among the authors Jonathan P. How, h-index 91 (Draper Laboratory)
Context. Flying robots the size of an insect usually need cameras in the room and an external computer to stay stable, so they cannot leave the lab.
The team built a 1.29-gram flapping-wing robot that hovers and follows paths using only sensors and computing carried on board, with centimeter-level position accuracy. A person gives high-level commands and the robot handles the rest. In a 30-second flight outside the motion-capture lab, it avoided obstacles and landed on a sunflower. It has the top quality score in our data (5 of 5) and a senior author with an h-index of 91; its full card is in Aerospace below.
AEROSPACE
47 of the 309 new aerospace papers were published this week.
Biomimetic flight and propulsion mechanismsstable
Topic share over 3 years: −13%
What it is about. Engineers copy how birds and insects fly to build small aircraft that can flap, hover and turn in tight spaces. Think of a drone that moves like a bee rather than a helicopter.
Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
Science Robotics · Published 18 Nov 2026  Journal  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Hsiao Yi-Hsuan and 8 others · Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cornell University (United States) · among the authors Jonathan P. How, h-index 91 (Draper Laboratory)
CONTEXTReal insects fly easily through dense plants. Robots of similar size depend on external sensors and computers, which limits them to special test rooms.
WHAT THEY DOThey built a 1.29-gram robot with its own sensors, software that estimates its position, and a low-level flight controller. On top, a hierarchical controller lets a human operator give simple directions.
RESULTThe robot reached centimeter-scale position accuracy. In a 30-second flight outside a motion-capture system it avoided obstacles and landed on a sunflower.
WHY IT MATTERSIt suggests tiny drones could one day work in real places, such as search-and-rescue or precision farming, without a lab around them.
LEO Satellite Traffic Prediction for Remote Sensing Data Using Dynamic Topology Index-Based TGCN
Aerospace · Published 17 Nov 2026  Journal
Xidian University forecasts data traffic in low-orbit satellite networks whose links keep changing, tested on a simulated 66-satellite Iridium constellation.
ArcticDEM Workbench for Traceable Multitemporal Elevation Change Analysis
Computers · Published 20 Nov 2026  Journal
Free software that compares satellite height maps of the Arctic over time while recording every processing choice, tried on a 2017 landslide in Alaska.
ENERGY
122 of the 899 new energy papers were published this week.
Organic Electronics and Photovoltaicsdeclining
Topic share over 3 years: −27%
What it is about. Organic solar cells use carbon-based plastics instead of silicon. They can be light, flexible and printed, and researchers are working to make them more efficient and stable.
Bayesian parameter estimation for predictive modeling of illumination-dependent current-voltage curves
PRX Energy · Published 18 Nov 2026  Journal  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Eunchi Kim, Thomas Kirchartz · among the authors Thomas Kirchartz, h-index 82 (Forschungszentrum Jülich)
CONTEXTScientists judge a solar cell by fitting a physics model to its measurements and reading off material properties. Machine learning makes this fast, but nobody can easily tell whether those properties are right.
WHAT THEY DOThey propose 'predictive power' as a check: a model and its fitted values should reproduce data that were not used in the fit. They test this on an organic solar cell measured under different light levels, changing how the model treats leakage current and what it tries to match.
RESULTPredictions under light conditions outside the fitting data depend on the model chosen, which shows which physical effects each model captures. A single measurement taken in the dark gives broad, uncertain estimates and less accurate predictions.
WHY IT MATTERSAs automated labs feed fitted values straight into optimization loops, a simple test like this can help stop wrong numbers from steering research.
Distinct Effects of Central and Terminal Acceptor Substitution in Y6-Derived Single-Component Organic Solar Cells
Chemistry of Materials · Published 18 Nov 2026  Journal
UNC Chapel Hill changes parts of a well-known solar molecule and finds the end pieces are far less forgiving to modify than the central piece.
Molecular Skeleton Engineering of Volatile Solid Additives Enables Dynamic Morphology Regulation for High-Performance Organic Solar Cells
ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces · Published 18 Nov 2026  Journal
An additive that evaporates after film formation helps arrange the active layer, reaching 20.14% efficiency versus 19.75% with a similar additive.
LLMS AND GENERATIVE AI
21 of the 175 new papers in this vertical were published this week.
Multimodal Machine Learning Applicationsemerging
Topic share over 3 years: +226%
What it is about. Multimodal AI handles several kinds of input at once, such as pictures and text. It is what lets an assistant describe a photo or answer questions about a chart.
Generalizing Vision-Language Models to Novel Domains: A Comprehensive Survey
ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing Communications and Applications · Published 20 Nov 2026  Review  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Xinyao Li and 5 others · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, University of Technology Sydney, Tongji University (China, Australia) · among the authors Lei Zhu, h-index 60 (Tongji University)
CONTEXTVision-language models learn from huge amounts of web images and captions and can handle new tasks without extra training. They often do worse on specialized fields, where images look different from the web.
WHAT THEY DOThis survey sorts the methods for adapting these models to new domains into three families: changing the prompt, changing some of the model's parameters, or changing its internal features. It also reviews common benchmarks, compares reported results, and discusses how these models relate to newer multimodal large language models such as DeepSeek-VL.
WHY IT MATTERSIt offers a map for anyone trying to use general image-and-text AI in specialized settings, where most of the practical value and difficulty may lie.
Artificial intelligence and machine learning in Islamic banking: insights using lexicon and machine learning-based models
Journal of Islamic marketing · Published 20 Nov 2026  Journal
Five text-analysis models read annual reports of 71 Islamic banks in 16 countries (2015–2023) and find a mostly positive tone about AI.
PVminer: a domain-specific tool to detect the patient voice in patient generated data
Scientific Reports · Published 19 Nov 2026  Journal
Yale and Texas State build language models trained on patient messages to tag what patients express, including social factors that affect their health.
CYBERSECURITY
63 of the 461 new cybersecurity papers were published this week.
Digital Media Forensic Detectionstrong growth
Topic share over 3 years: +86%
What it is about. Media forensics checks whether a photo or video has been edited or faked. It is used by newsrooms, courts and platforms fighting manipulated content.
State of the art in image forgery detection using large language models to identify gaps for improving accuracy and reducing hallucinations
Discover Artificial Intelligence · Published 19 Nov 2026  Review  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Thobeka Langa, Hein S. Venter · University of Pretoria (South Africa) · among the authors Hein S. Venter, h-index 34
CONTEXTLarge language models combined with image analysis are now used to tell real photos from manipulated ones. Many studies show they sometimes 'hallucinate': they give confident, plausible but wrong answers.
WHAT THEY DOThe authors review current approaches that use large language models for image forgery detection. They look at the main building blocks of these systems and at the issues that cause hallucinations and lower accuracy, and they list gaps and directions for future work.
WHY IT MATTERSIf AI is going to vouch for whether an image is real, its own mistakes become a security problem; this review points to where those mistakes come from.
IronBus: A Decentralized Trusted Bus for Accelerators - A HW-SW Co-Designed Trusted Acceleration Interface
ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization · Published 18 Nov 2026  Journal
TU Munich proposes protected direct channels between cloud AI chips such as GPUs, with security checks at each chip instead of a central host.
A multi-layer deep feature selection and meta-ensemble learning framework for cross-platform malware detection
Scientific Reports · Published 17 Nov 2026  Journal
One system combines twelve detectors to spot malicious software on both Windows and Android, evaluated on six public datasets.
ROBOTICS AND AUTOMATION
37 of the 259 new robotics papers were published this week.
Robotics and Sensor-Based Localizationgrowing
Topic share over 3 years: +18%
What it is about. Robots need to know where they are and what is around them. Laser sensors called LiDAR measure distances by bouncing light off objects, like a bat using echoes.
Blind spot minimization through optimized LiDAR placement
Scientific Reports · Published 20 Nov 2026  Journal  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Melisa Oshaini Arukgoda and 4 others · Singapore University of Technology and Design, University of Moratuwa, Kyung Hee University (Singapore, Sri Lanka, South Korea) · among the authors Mohan Rajesh Elara, h-index 38 (Singapore University of Technology and Design)
CONTEXTWhere sensors sit on a large robot decides what it can and cannot see. Past work mostly maximized total coverage, without favoring the areas that matter most for safety.
WHAT THEY DOThey built a simulation to place 2D LiDAR sensors on large, oddly shaped robots, with a score that rewards seeing high-priority areas. Three search methods inspired by nature and physics (genetic algorithm, particle swarm, simulated annealing) look for the best layout, judged by five blind-spot measures.
RESULTThe method was tested on five robots of very different shapes, with two to five sensors each, over 10 independent runs per setup.
WHY IT MATTERSFewer blind spots in the right places can make large robots safer around people without adding more sensors.
Model-Selection Logic for Tendon-Driven Systems: A Review
Machines · Published 18 Nov 2026  Review
University of Genoa and the Italian Institute of Technology explain how to choose the right model for robots moved by cables, like tendons in a hand.
Post-amputation low back pain is associated with reduced walking capacity and performance one year after bone-anchored limb implantation
Disability and Rehabilitation · Published 19 Nov 2026  Journal
In 54 people with a prosthetic leg fixed to the bone, more back pain went with walking less well one year after surgery.

In short: LLMs and generative AI remain far ahead in research growth, while cybersecurity shows the strongest jump in developer activity on GitHub. Energy is the only vertical losing momentum this year, even though it had the most new papers this week.
WORDS OF THE WEEK
h-index — A measure of a researcher's influence: an h-index of 30 means 30 papers each cited at least 30 times.
Motion capture — A room full of cameras that tracks an object's exact position, like the setups used to animate film characters.
Vision-language model — An AI trained on images and their captions, so it can talk about what it sees.
Hallucination — When an AI gives a confident answer that sounds right but is wrong, like a witness who fills memory gaps by guessing.
LiDAR — A sensor that measures distance with laser pulses, building a map of the surroundings; many robot vacuums use one.
WORTH WATCHING
Watch whether tiny flying robots like this week's MIT design can add onboard planning and power, as the authors suggest. In AI, the rise of multimodal models comes with a growing body of work on their errors, from new domains to image forensics: reliability may become the main story in this vertical.
